title: Glacial Lance Ritualist Build Guide: Lance Pierce, Offering Buffs and Endgame
summary: 0.5.4 spear-cold toolkit: Glacial Lance gains damage and pierce via Ritualist offerings, Spear Field lays ground buffs. Covers lance hits, offering timing, spear-set swap and budget tiers.
description: Path of Exile 2 Glacial Lance Ritualist guide for 0.5.4: lance pierce, offering buffs, spear-set swap, defense boundaries and real video timestamps.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: Huntress Ritualist piercing a frozen pack with Glacial Lance in combat

sections.title: Build Overview
paragraphs: Glacial Lance Ritualist is the Huntress spear-cold toolkit: Glacial Lance thrusts the spear and pierces a line of enemies, while the Ritualist ascendancy's Offering grants you and your sacrificed offering damage, pierce and survival. Spear Field lays a ground buff zone.

This route is strong from leveling: Glacial Lance is usable early and Offering stabilizes pierce and cold damage. It does not burn resources like a pure caster, but it leans on Accuracy and spear affixes.

This guide is stage-based: first when to pop Offering and how to swap spear sets, then gear, passives, set swap and budget tiers. All client numbers and mechanics are flagged for PC verification; unverified DPS is not stated as fact.
bullets: Mapping is Glacial Lance pierce + Spear Field buff, near one-button.
Bossing closes with the Offering damage window plus spear-set swap.
Accuracy and spear affixes are real bottlenecks that need handling.

sections.title: Pros and Cons
pros: Lance pierce clears packs very efficiently; mapping feels great.
Ritualist Offering gives a clear damage window and clean boss finish.
No resource cost; sustain pressure is low.
Works on a low budget early and transitions smoothly; beginner-friendly.
cons: Low Accuracy causes many pierce misses.
Spear affixes (cold/spear damage) are not native and must be stacked.
Bosses that move a lot lower pierce hit rate.
When the offered sacrifice dies you temporarily lose the buff; replenish it.

sections.title: How the Loop Reads: Spear Field → Glacial Lance → Offering
paragraphs: Mapping loop: lay Spear Field first, then repeat Glacial Lance through packs; you mostly just position on the line. This is why the community calls it one-button mapping.

Boss loop: lay Spear Field on the boss path, pierce with Glacial Lance, then open the Offering damage window once its resource is full and swap spear sets as needed (one cold, one armor-break/physical).
Offering usually means you summon and sacrifice an offering for a buff, not a free mechanic; verify against the skill description and client, do not treat it as a hidden extra system.
bullets: Mapping = Spear Field + Glacial Lance pierce.
Boss = buff zone → pierce → Offering window.
Spear-set swap is the key damage supplement.

steps.label: Levels 1–14
body: Start with Glacial Lance. It is usable very early and is your real mapping skill; do not force Offering yet — resource and gear are not ready.

steps.label: Levels 15–29
body: Add Spear Field as a ground buff and start taking Accuracy/cold-damage/life nodes. Keep Glacial Lance as the core.

steps.label: Levels 30–42 — Ritualist Unlocks
body: Pick Ritualist and take Offering nodes. The Offering window now gives boss burst.

steps.label: Levels 43–60 — Early Maps
body: Run pierce + Offering on a low budget. Cap resistances, fix Accuracy and life, keep the buff zone up on rares.

steps.label: Level 60+ — Endgame Prep
body: Move into budget upgrades: spear cold damage, Accuracy, crit and Chaos Res. Only chase high-end gear after the upgrade-priority checklist passes.

steps.label: Ritualist — First Nodes
body: Pick Ritualist. Prioritize Offering nodes so the damage window reliably provides burst; this is the precondition for the build.

steps.label: Accuracy & Defense Check
body: If T15+ Accuracy is short or survival is shaky, do not trade Offering/cold nodes for pure damage; secure Accuracy and Chaos Res first.

steps.label: Campaign
body: Only take nodes supporting spear/cold damage and Accuracy; do not pre-path to crit wheels.

steps.label: Early Maps
body: Switch into the pierce variant; prioritize life, Accuracy, cold damage and Chaos Res.

steps.label: Endgame
body: After defense and Accuracy are solved, invest in crit/spear-damage wheels; compare gear states at the same tier.

recommendations: Pick a base that boosts spear level and cold/spear damage; enough sockets for Glacial Lance links. Consider two: one cold, one armor-break/physical.

sections.title: Mapping
paragraphs: Lay Spear Field first, then repeat Glacial Lance through packs; you only position on the line. Trash does not need Offering; stopping to trigger slows you down.
Once clear slows, upgrade the spear first. Keep some survival (resist/life/kite) active so mapping never stalls.
bullets: Spear Field + pierce is the whole mapping rhythm.
Reactively upgrade the spear when clear slows.

sections.title: Bossing
paragraphs: Bossing is a sequence: lay Spear Field on the boss path, pierce with Glacial Lance, then open the Offering damage window once its resource is full and swap spear sets (cold/armor-break) as needed. Blood Hunt cleans up on phase swaps.
If pierce whiffs often, the problem is Accuracy, not the spear. When the boss moves a lot, place Spear Field on the narrow path it must cross, not at its feet.
bullets: Whiff = fix Accuracy and placement, not swap weapon.

sections.title: Budget Tiers: Real Cheap vs Luxury Differences
paragraphs: Cheap: a low-budget spear plus solved Accuracy/resistances/life, clearing and bossing most content on pierce + Offering. It changes whether you can play, not the damage number.
Luxury: high spear level, specific Uniques, capped Chaos Res and crit, raising both lance resolution and survival. It changes ceiling and error margin, not turning cheap into a different build.
Mirror tier only after you have verified cheap/luxury pass and client numbers confirm; do not sacrifice Chaos Res and Accuracy for DPS.
bullets: Cheap first: life, resistances, Accuracy, a decent spear.
Luxury later: spear level, cold damage, crit.
Mirror tier never breaks the defense floor.

items.question: What level do I start using Glacial Lance?
answer: Usable very early; it is the real mapping skill. Offering waits for Ritualist and resource.

items.question: I swapped a better spear but still whiff a lot?
answer: The lance depends on Accuracy for pierce hits, not the spear alone; fix Accuracy first.
bullets: Record a boss fight and check hit rate.

items.question: Can I play SSF?
answer: Yes; low-budget pierce + Offering map and boss most content in SSF. Luxury Uniques are a ceiling, not a gate.
